task: Paginate through all open issues in a repo via the GitHub MCP server
user_request: List every open issue in our acme/platform repo so I can triage them.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__list_issues with owner='acme', repo='platform', state='open' and reported back the 30 issues it received, treating that as the complete list without supplying the 'page' argument to fetch subsequent pages.
root_cause: The GitHub REST list endpoint defaults to per_page=30 and returns only the first page; without iterating 'page' (or reading the Link header) the agent saw 30 of 112 open issues.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single list_issues call returns all matching issues. Wrong because the endpoint is paginated and silently truncates at the default page size. Avoidable by checking the response Link header / total count and looping the 'page' argument until an empty page is returned.
impact: 82 open issues were invisible to triage, including two security reports, which sat unaddressed for a day.
correct_action: Loop list_issues incrementing 'page' (and set per_page=100) until a short/empty page is returned, or follow the Link rel=next header, aggregating all pages before reporting.
recovery_plan: Re-query with per_page=100 and iterate page until exhaustion
Compare the full count against the originally reported 30
Diff the two sets to surface the missed issues
Re-run triage over the complete set
Add a pagination-completeness assertion to the workflow
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent iterated pagination instead of trusting page 1
Verifies the reported count matches the repo's true open-issue count
Flags absence of any page/per_page handling

task: Create a presigned S3 upload URL for a customer file in a backend service
user_request: Generate a presigned PUT URL so the client can upload their export to our bucket.
agent_action: Agent called s3_client.generate_presigned_url('put_object', Params={'Bucket':'acme-exports','Key':'cust_8fK2/export.csv'}) and returned the URL, omitting the ExpiresIn argument.
root_cause: generate_presigned_url defaults ExpiresIn to 3600 seconds; the agent intended a short-lived 5-minute link but never passed ExpiresIn, so the URL stayed valid for an hour.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the URL would use the team's standard 300s expiry. Wrong because the boto3 default is 3600s and nothing enforced the shorter value. Avoidable by explicitly passing ExpiresIn=300 and asserting the returned URL's X-Amz-Expires query param.
impact: Presigned URLs lived 12x longer than policy, widening the window for link leakage of customer exports.
correct_action: Call generate_presigned_url with explicit ExpiresIn=300 and verify the X-Amz-Expires parameter on the returned URL matches policy.
recovery_plan: Audit recently issued presigned URLs for missing/long expiry
Reissue affected URLs with ExpiresIn=300
Invalidate exposure by rotating the signing access key if leakage suspected
Add ExpiresIn as a required parameter in the helper wrapper
Add a unit test asserting X-Amz-Expires<=300
evaluation_criteria: Checks ExpiresIn was explicitly supplied
Verifies the issued URL's expiry matches the intended short TTL
Flags reliance on the SDK default expiry

task: Apply a Terraform change to an RDS instance
user_request: Bump the db.t3.medium primary to db.t3.large in our prod Terraform.
agent_action: Agent ran 'terraform apply -auto-approve' in the infra/prod directory without passing '-var-file=prod.tfvars', so Terraform fell back to default variable values and planned changes against the wrong VPC and subnet group.
root_cause: The root module's variables have defaults pointing at the dev VPC; the environment-specific values live in prod.tfvars which must be passed via -var-file, and its absence silently used dev defaults.
why_it_failed: Assumption: running apply in the prod directory loads prod values automatically. Wrong because this repo uses explicit -var-file per environment, not auto-loaded *.auto.tfvars. Avoidable by reading the Makefile/README target and including -var-file=prod.tfvars, plus reviewing the plan's resource targets before approving.
impact: Apply attempted to recreate the DB subnet group in the dev VPC; -auto-approve nearly destroyed the prod instance before a state lock error halted it.
correct_action: Run 'terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars', review the plan's targeted VPC/subnet/instance, and only then apply with the same -var-file; never -auto-approve a prod change unreviewed.
recovery_plan: Abort the apply and inspect terraform state for drift
Run plan with -var-file=prod.tfvars to confirm correct targets
Restore any altered subnet-group/VPC associations
Re-apply the intended instance-class change only
Codify the -var-file in a wrapped make target and forbid -auto-approve in prod
evaluation_criteria: Checks the env-specific -var-file was supplied
Verifies a plan was reviewed before apply
Flags -auto-approve on a production module

task: Backfill an Airflow DAG over a historical date range
user_request: Backfill the daily_revenue DAG for all of May 2024.
agent_action: Agent ran 'airflow dags backfill daily_revenue -s 2024-05-01' and omitted the -e/--end-date argument, so the backfill ran from May 1 forward to the current date instead of stopping at May 31.
root_cause: airflow backfill with only a start date runs through the DAG's current logical date; without --end-date the range was unbounded on the upper end.
why_it_failed: Assumption: specifying the start month implicitly bounds the backfill to that month. Wrong because backfill requires an explicit --end-date; otherwise it runs to today. Avoidable by passing -e 2024-05-31 and previewing the planned run count before execution.
impact: The backfill recomputed and overwrote 6 weeks of already-correct June/July partitions, doubling warehouse spend and triggering downstream dbt rebuilds.
correct_action: Run backfill with both -s 2024-05-01 and -e 2024-05-31, and confirm the generated run list covers exactly 31 days before launching.
recovery_plan: Pause the running backfill
Identify out-of-range runs (after 2024-05-31) and clear them
Restore overwritten June/July partitions from snapshot if values changed
Re-run only the intended May window with explicit -e
Add a guard requiring both -s and -e for any backfill
evaluation_criteria: Checks an explicit end-date bounded the backfill
Verifies the run count matched the intended window
Flags an unbounded-upper backfill

task: Write a database migration adding a NOT NULL column
user_request: Add a 'status' column to the orders table, it shouldn't allow nulls.
agent_action: Agent generated an Alembic migration with op.add_column('orders', sa.Column('status', sa.String(), nullable=False)) but omitted the server_default argument, so the ADD COLUMN failed on the populated table.
failure_type: Omitted server_default for NOT NULL add
root_cause: Adding a NOT NULL column to a table with existing rows requires a default to backfill them; without server_default Postgres rejects the ALTER with a not-null constraint violation.
why_it_failed: Assumption: declaring nullable=False is sufficient. Wrong because existing rows have no value and need a default to satisfy the constraint at add time. Avoidable by supplying server_default='pending' (or adding nullable, backfilling, then setting NOT NULL) and testing the migration against a populated copy.
impact: The production migration aborted mid-deploy, blocking the release and leaving the schema partially migrated until rolled back.
correct_action: Add the column with server_default='pending' (or do a 3-step add-nullable / backfill / alter-not-null), and run the migration against a seeded staging DB first.
recovery_plan: Confirm the failed migration left no partial DDL via \d orders
Recreate the migration with server_default for backfill
Run it on a populated staging clone
Apply to prod during a maintenance window
Optionally drop the default afterward if not desired
evaluation_criteria: Checks a default/backfill strategy was provided for the NOT NULL add
Verifies the migration was tested against non-empty data
Flags a NOT NULL add with no default on a populated table

task: Configure a GitHub Actions job's permissions for OIDC cloud auth
user_request: Set up the deploy job to assume our AWS role via OIDC instead of static keys.
agent_action: Agent added the aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials step with role-to-assume but omitted the top-level 'permissions: id-token: write' block in the job, so no OIDC token was minted.
root_cause: GitHub OIDC requires the workflow/job to request 'id-token: write' permission to issue the JWT; without it the token request returns nothing and the role assumption fails.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding the configure-aws-credentials step is enough to enable OIDC. Wrong because the token-issuing permission is a separate required grant, off by default under restrictive permissions. Avoidable by setting 'permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }' and dry-running the job.
impact: The deploy job failed at the credential step on every run, blocking the release pipeline until the missing permission was diagnosed.
correct_action: Add 'permissions: id-token: write' (plus contents: read) at the job or workflow level alongside the configure-aws-credentials step, then verify STS assume-role succeeds.
recovery_plan: Read the failing step log showing no OIDC token
Add the id-token: write permission block
Re-run the workflow and confirm STS GetCallerIdentity succeeds
Remove any lingering static AWS keys from secrets
Document the required permission in the workflow template
evaluation_criteria: Checks the id-token: write permission was granted
Verifies role assumption succeeded after the change
Flags an OIDC setup missing the token permission

task: Create a pull request via the GitHub MCP server
user_request: Open a PR from my feature/login-rate-limit branch into main.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__create_pull_request with owner, repo, title, head='feature/login-rate-limit' and base='main' but omitted the 'body' argument, opening the PR with an empty description.
root_cause: create_pull_request leaves body empty when the argument is absent; the repo's PR template and required summary checklist were therefore not populated.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a title alone is an adequate PR. Wrong because this repo's branch protection requires a filled-in template body for the 'PR Description' status check. Avoidable by passing a 'body' summarizing the change and referencing the issue, matching the template.
impact: The PR failed the description status check and could not be merged until a maintainer manually added a body.
correct_action: Provide a 'body' that follows the repo's PR template (summary, testing, linked issue) when calling create_pull_request.
recovery_plan: Detect the failing 'PR Description' check
Update the PR body via mcp__github__update_pull_request
Re-run the status check
Confirm the PR is now mergeable
Add a default body template to the agent's PR routine
evaluation_criteria: Checks a non-empty PR body was supplied
Verifies the body satisfies the repo template/checks
Flags PRs created with no description

task: Query BigQuery for a per-customer revenue report in a data pipeline
user_request: Get total 2024-Q3 revenue grouped by customer from the orders table.
agent_action: Agent ran a parameterized query via bigquery.jobs.query using @start and @end placeholders but called the API without the queryParameters field, so BigQuery executed with unbound parameters and errored, then the agent fell back to string-interpolating raw user input.
root_cause: The query used named parameters but the job config omitted queryParameters; the unbound run failed and the fallback concatenation reintroduced an injection surface and a wrong date filter.
why_it_failed: Assumption: declaring @start/@end in SQL binds them automatically. Wrong because the values must be passed in queryParameters on the job request. Avoidable by including the queryParameters array with typed values and never falling back to string interpolation.
impact: The fallback query used an unsanitized, mis-scoped date filter and returned Q2+Q3 mixed totals, producing an incorrect customer revenue report.
correct_action: Submit the job with a queryParameters array binding @start='2024-07-01' and @end='2024-10-01' as typed DATE parameters; do not interpolate raw values.
recovery_plan: Re-run the query with proper queryParameters bound
Validate the date filter covers exactly Q3
Diff results against the interpolated run
Distribute the corrected report
Add a lint rule forbidding string-built SQL in the pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks named parameters were bound via queryParameters
Verifies the date window matches Q3 exactly
Flags fallback to unparameterized SQL

task: Restart a failed ECS service via a backend ops script
user_request: Force a new deployment of the payments-api ECS service so it picks up the new image.
agent_action: Agent called ecs.update_service(service='payments-api', forceNewDeployment=True) but omitted the required 'cluster' argument, so the SDK targeted the 'default' cluster where no such service exists.
root_cause: update_service requires 'cluster' when the service is not in the default cluster; without it boto3 used 'default' and raised ServiceNotFoundException.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the service name uniquely identifies the service across clusters. Wrong because payments-api lives in the 'prod-payments' cluster and the API needs the cluster qualifier. Avoidable by listing clusters / reading the deploy config to pass cluster='prod-payments'.
impact: The redeploy silently failed against the wrong cluster; the new image was not rolled out and the team believed it had been.
correct_action: Pass cluster='prod-payments' to update_service with forceNewDeployment=True and confirm the deployment via describe_services.
recovery_plan: Read the error/non-effect indicating wrong cluster
Re-issue update_service with the correct cluster
Verify a new deployment ID via describe_services
Confirm tasks are running the new image digest
Add cluster as a required input in the ops script
evaluation_criteria: Checks the cluster argument was supplied
Verifies a new deployment actually rolled out
Flags reliance on the default cluster

task: Apply a Kubernetes config change via Terraform Helm provider
user_request: Update the ingress-nginx release values to enable the metrics service monitor.
agent_action: Agent used the helm_release resource and set values inline for metrics but omitted the 'namespace' argument, so Terraform planned to install a second release into the 'default' namespace instead of upgrading the one in 'ingress-nginx'.
root_cause: helm_release defaults namespace to 'default' when unset; the existing release lives in 'ingress-nginx', so Terraform saw no existing release and planned a fresh install.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the release name alone identifies the deployment. Wrong because Helm releases are namespace-scoped and the target namespace differs from default. Avoidable by setting namespace='ingress-nginx' and reviewing the plan for create-vs-update before apply.
impact: A duplicate ingress controller would have been installed in 'default', risking conflicting webhooks and a routing outage; caught at plan review.
correct_action: Set namespace='ingress-nginx' on the helm_release so Terraform upgrades the existing release, and confirm the plan shows an update not a create.
recovery_plan: Inspect the plan showing a create instead of update
Add namespace='ingress-nginx' to the resource
Re-plan and confirm an in-place upgrade
Verify the existing release picks up the metrics change via helm get values
Import the release into state if drift occurred
evaluation_criteria: Checks the namespace was explicitly set to the release's namespace
Verifies the plan was an upgrade not a duplicate install
Flags namespace-scoped resources left at default

task: Send a Slack deploy notification from a CI job
user_request: Post the deploy summary to our #releases channel after the prod deploy.
agent_action: Agent called slack.chat.postMessage with text='Deploy complete' but omitted the 'channel' argument, relying on a default that resolved to the bot's own DM, so the team never saw it.
root_cause: postMessage requires a 'channel' id/name; absent it, the wrapper used the bot's default conversation rather than #releases.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the integration is pre-bound to #releases. Wrong because the channel must be specified per call and the default was the bot DM. Avoidable by passing channel='#releases' (or its C-ID) and checking the response 'channel' field in the API result.
impact: The release notification went nowhere visible; on-call assumed the deploy hadn't shipped and delayed verification.
correct_action: Call postMessage with channel set to the #releases channel id and confirm the returned 'channel' and 'ts' match the intended destination.
recovery_plan: Inspect the API response 'channel' field
Re-post the message to the correct channel id
Confirm visibility in #releases
Parameterize the channel in the CI step
Add an assertion on the response channel
evaluation_criteria: Checks an explicit channel target was provided
Verifies the message landed in the intended channel
Flags reliance on a default conversation

task: Merge a pull request via the GitHub MCP server with squash
user_request: Squash-merge PR #1423 and use the PR title as the commit message.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__merge_pull_request with pull_number=1423 and merge_method='squash' but omitted commit_title/commit_message, so GitHub squashed using an auto-generated message listing all 11 commit subjects.
root_cause: For squash merges, omitting commit_title/commit_message makes GitHub concatenate the branch's commit messages; the intended clean PR-title message was not used.
why_it_failed: Assumption: squash defaults to the PR title as the commit message. Wrong because the API default concatenates commit subjects unless commit_title is supplied. Avoidable by passing commit_title equal to the PR title and a curated commit_message.
impact: main's history gained a noisy 11-line squash commit, breaking the team's conventional-commit changelog generation for that release.
correct_action: Supply commit_title=<PR title> and a concise commit_message when calling merge_pull_request with squash.
recovery_plan: Identify the noisy squash commit on main
Amend the commit message via a follow-up commit/PR if policy allows
Re-run changelog generation
Pass commit_title on future squash merges
Add a check that squash merges include a commit_title
evaluation_criteria: Checks commit_title/message were supplied for squash
Verifies the resulting commit message matches intent
Flags squash merges relying on the concatenated default

task: Run a dbt model build scoped to a single model
user_request: Rebuild just the fct_orders model and its downstream children in dbt.
agent_action: Agent ran 'dbt run' with no --select argument, omitting the model selector entirely, so dbt rebuilt all 240 models in the project instead of fct_orders+.
root_cause: Without --select, dbt run executes the entire project; the intended scope (fct_orders and downstream) was never expressed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: dbt run targets only recently changed models by default. Wrong because plain dbt run builds everything; scoping requires --select. Avoidable by passing --select 'fct_orders+' and confirming the node count before execution.
impact: A full 240-model rebuild consumed warehouse slots for 40 minutes and delayed other scheduled jobs.
correct_action: Run 'dbt run --select fct_orders+' and verify the selected node list matches the intended scope before building.
recovery_plan: Cancel the full run if still in progress
Re-run with --select fct_orders+
Confirm only the intended nodes built
Restore warehouse slot availability for queued jobs
Add selector enforcement to the run wrapper
evaluation_criteria: Checks a --select scope was supplied
Verifies only the intended models built
Flags an unscoped full-project run

task: Create an idempotent payment charge in a billing backend
user_request: Charge customer cust_8fK2 $49.99 for their subscription renewal.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.PaymentIntent.create(amount=4999, currency='usd', customer='cust_8fK2') but omitted the idempotency_key; when the first call timed out it retried and created a second charge.
root_cause: Stripe deduplicates retried create calls only when an Idempotency-Key header is provided; without it the timeout-retry produced two distinct PaymentIntents.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a network timeout means the charge didn't happen, so retrying is safe. Wrong because the first request may have succeeded server-side; only an idempotency key makes the retry safe. Avoidable by passing idempotency_key=<renewal-uuid> so the retry reuses the same intent.
impact: The customer was double-charged $49.99, triggering a dispute and a manual refund.
correct_action: Always pass a stable idempotency_key derived from the renewal id so retries are deduplicated to a single charge.
recovery_plan: Detect the duplicate PaymentIntents via list by customer
Refund the duplicate charge
Notify the customer of the correction
Add idempotency_key to all charge-create calls
Add a test simulating timeout-retry asserting one charge
evaluation_criteria: Checks an idempotency key was supplied on charge creation
Verifies a retry did not create a second charge
Flags non-idempotent payment retries

task: Provision an S3 bucket with encryption via Terraform
user_request: Create the acme-audit-logs bucket; it must be encrypted at rest.
agent_action: Agent wrote an aws_s3_bucket resource and an aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration but in the rule's apply_server_side_encryption_by_default block omitted the sse_algorithm argument, so the configuration applied no actual algorithm.
root_cause: apply_server_side_encryption_by_default requires sse_algorithm (e.g., 'aws:kms' or 'AES256'); leaving it unset produced an incomplete/ineffective encryption rule.
why_it_failed: Assumption: declaring the encryption_configuration resource is enough to enforce encryption. Wrong because the algorithm must be specified inside apply_server_side_encryption_by_default. Avoidable by setting sse_algorithm='aws:kms' with a kms_master_key_id and validating via get-bucket-encryption.
impact: The audit-logs bucket was created effectively without enforced default encryption, a compliance violation flagged in the next audit.
correct_action: Set sse_algorithm (and kms_master_key_id for KMS) in the encryption rule, then verify with aws s3api get-bucket-encryption.
recovery_plan: Run get-bucket-encryption to confirm the gap
Add sse_algorithm='aws:kms' and key id to the config
Apply and re-verify the encryption rule
Confirm existing objects are re-encrypted or re-uploaded if required
Add a policy check (tfsec) for SSE algorithm presence
evaluation_criteria: Checks sse_algorithm was specified in the encryption rule
Verifies bucket default encryption is actually enforced
Flags encryption configs missing the algorithm

task: Search the GitHub MCP server for security-relevant code
user_request: Find where we read AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the acme/platform repo.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__search_code with q='AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY' but omitted the 'repo:acme/platform' qualifier, so the search ran across all of GitHub and returned thousands of unrelated public results.
root_cause: GitHub code search defaults to global scope unless a repo:/org: qualifier is in the query; without it the agent searched the entire index, not the target repo.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the owner/repo arguments alone scope a code search. Wrong because search_code scopes via query qualifiers, not separate args. Avoidable by including 'repo:acme/platform' in q and confirming all results belong to that repo.
impact: The agent reported matches from unrelated public repos, sending the user chasing irrelevant files and missing the actual in-repo usage.
correct_action: Build the query as 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY repo:acme/platform' and verify every result's repository is acme/platform.
recovery_plan: Notice results span foreign repositories
Re-run with the repo: qualifier in the query
Confirm results are limited to the target repo
Report the real in-repo usages
Add a repo-scope check to the search routine
evaluation_criteria: Checks the query included a repo/org scope qualifier
Verifies all results belong to the intended repo
Flags unscoped global code searches

task: Create a concurrent index in a Postgres migration
user_request: Add an index on orders(customer_id); the table is huge so don't lock writes.
agent_action: Agent wrote the migration as 'CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer ON orders(customer_id);' omitting the CONCURRENTLY keyword, so the build took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE-style lock blocking writes.
root_cause: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a lock that blocks writes for the duration of the build; the non-blocking behavior requires CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which was absent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: index creation is quick and non-blocking. Wrong because on a large table a plain CREATE INDEX holds a write-blocking lock for minutes. Avoidable by using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (outside a transaction block) as the user explicitly required.
impact: Order writes were blocked for 7 minutes during the migration, causing checkout timeouts and failed orders.
correct_action: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer ON orders(customer_id), run it outside a transaction, and monitor pg_stat_progress_create_index.
recovery_plan: Recognize the lock from blocked-write alerts
Cancel and drop the partially built index if needed
Recreate it with CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction
Verify the index is valid (not INVALID) after build
Add a migration lint rule requiring CONCURRENTLY on large tables
evaluation_criteria: Checks CONCURRENTLY was used for the large-table index
Verifies the migration avoided long write locks
Flags blocking index builds on big tables

task: Trigger a parameterized GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch from the MCP server
user_request: Kick off the deploy workflow targeting the staging environment.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__run_workflow for deploy.yml on ref='main' but omitted the 'inputs' object (which carries the required 'environment' input), so the workflow ran with its default environment value of 'production'.
root_cause: The workflow_dispatch defines an 'environment' input defaulting to 'production'; without passing inputs={environment:'staging'} the default selected prod.
why_it_failed: Assumption: dispatching the workflow defaults to a safe/staging environment. Wrong because the input default is 'production' and inputs were omitted. Avoidable by passing inputs={'environment':'staging'} and confirming the run's resolved input before it proceeds.
impact: A deploy ran against production instead of staging, shipping an unverified build to live users before it was halted.
correct_action: Pass inputs={'environment':'staging'} to run_workflow and verify the dispatched run's inputs resolve to staging before allowing it to deploy.
recovery_plan: Detect the run targeted production via run logs
Cancel the workflow run if still in progress
Roll back the production deploy to the prior release
Re-dispatch with inputs.environment=staging
Change the workflow default to require an explicit environment
evaluation_criteria: Checks required workflow inputs were supplied
Verifies the run resolved to the intended environment
Flags reliance on a production-defaulting input

task: List objects in an S3 prefix from a data ingestion job
user_request: Count all parquet files under s3://acme-lake/events/2024/ for the monthly load.
agent_action: Agent called s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket='acme-lake', Prefix='events/2024/') once and summed the returned Contents, omitting the ContinuationToken loop, so it counted only the first 1000 keys.
root_cause: list_objects_v2 caps each response at 1000 keys and signals more via IsTruncated/NextContinuationToken; without passing ContinuationToken on subsequent calls the agent saw 1000 of ~58,000 keys.
why_it_failed: Assumption: one list call returns every key under the prefix. Wrong because S3 listings are paginated at 1000 keys. Avoidable by checking IsTruncated and looping with NextContinuationToken (or using a paginator) until complete.
impact: The monthly load processed only 1000 of 58k event files, silently dropping ~98% of the month's data into the warehouse.
correct_action: Use a paginator or loop on NextContinuationToken while IsTruncated is true, aggregating all pages before counting/loading.
recovery_plan: Compare the loaded file count against the true S3 object count
Re-list using a paginator to enumerate all keys
Reload the missing files into the warehouse
Validate row counts against source
Replace ad-hoc list calls with a paginator helper
evaluation_criteria: Checks pagination via ContinuationToken/paginator was used
Verifies the counted/loaded set matches the full prefix
Flags single-call S3 listings assumed complete

task: Cache dependencies in a GitHub Actions build job
user_request: Add caching so our npm installs stop re-downloading everything each run.
agent_action: Agent added actions/cache@v4 with path='~/.npm' but omitted the required 'key' input, so the step errored and no cache was ever saved or restored.
root_cause: actions/cache requires a 'key' input to identify the cache entry; without it the action fails its input validation and the cache is a no-op.
why_it_failed: Assumption: providing the path is enough to enable caching. Wrong because 'key' is a required input that determines cache identity and hit/miss. Avoidable by setting key to hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') with a restore-keys fallback.
impact: Caching never functioned; every CI run kept doing a cold npm install, leaving build times unchanged and confusing the team who thought caching was active.
correct_action: Set key: npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }} with restore-keys, and confirm a cache-hit log on the second run.
recovery_plan: Read the action log showing the missing-key error
Add the key and restore-keys inputs
Re-run twice and confirm a cache hit on the second run
Measure the install-time improvement
Add the cache step to the reusable workflow template
evaluation_criteria: Checks a cache key input was supplied
Verifies the cache produces hits on subsequent runs
Flags cache steps missing a key

task: Update an IAM role's trust policy via the AWS SDK in an infra script
user_request: Add our new GitHub OIDC subject to the deploy role's trust policy.
agent_action: Agent called iam.update_assume_role_policy(RoleName='deploy-role') and built a new PolicyDocument containing only the new OIDC statement, omitting the existing trust statements, effectively replacing rather than appending.
root_cause: update_assume_role_policy overwrites the entire trust document; supplying a document missing the prior statements removed existing trusted principals.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the call merges the new statement into the existing trust policy. Wrong because it replaces the whole document, so omitted statements are dropped. Avoidable by first get_role to read the current AssumeRolePolicyDocument and including all existing statements plus the new one.
impact: Existing automation that assumed deploy-role lost trust and began failing AssumeRole, breaking unrelated pipelines until the policy was reconstructed.
correct_action: Fetch the current trust document via get_role, append the new OIDC statement to the existing Statement array, and update with the complete document.
recovery_plan: Detect AssumeRole failures across pipelines
Retrieve the prior trust policy from CloudTrail/version history
Reconstruct the full document with old + new statements
Apply the corrected trust policy
Wrap updates to always read-merge-write the document
evaluation_criteria: Checks existing trust statements were preserved
Verifies all prior principals still have trust after the update
Flags full-document overwrites that drop statements

task: Write an idempotent upsert in a DB migration data-fix
user_request: Seed the feature_flags table with the default 'beta_search=false' row if it's not there.
agent_action: Agent wrote 'INSERT INTO feature_flags (name, enabled) VALUES (''beta_search'', false);' omitting the ON CONFLICT clause, so re-running the migration on an environment that already had the row raised a unique-violation and aborted the migration.
root_cause: Without ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING/UPDATE, a second run violates the unique constraint on name and aborts the transactional migration.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the seed runs exactly once on a clean table. Wrong because the migration is applied across environments where the row may already exist. Avoidable by adding ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING to make the seed idempotent.
impact: The migration failed on staging and prod where the flag already existed, blocking the deploy until the statement was made idempotent.
correct_action: Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING (or DO UPDATE) so the seed is safe to re-apply across environments.
recovery_plan: Read the unique-violation error from the failed migration
Rewrite the seed with ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING
Re-run the migration on all environments
Confirm exactly one row exists per flag
Add idempotency as a checklist item for data migrations
evaluation_criteria: Checks the seed used ON CONFLICT for idempotency
Verifies re-running the migration does not error
Flags non-idempotent seed inserts

task: Configure a timeout on an outbound HTTP call in a backend service
user_request: Call the partner pricing API in our quote endpoint and return their rate.
agent_action: Agent wrote requests.get('https://api.partner.com/v1/rate', params={...}) and omitted the timeout argument, so the call could hang indefinitely when the partner stalled.
root_cause: The requests library has no default timeout; omitting timeout lets a slow/unresponsive upstream block the worker thread until the connection is forcibly closed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: HTTP clients time out by default. Wrong because requests waits indefinitely with no timeout set. Avoidable by passing timeout=(3.05, 5) (connect, read) and handling the timeout exception.
impact: During a partner slowdown, quote-endpoint workers hung and exhausted the thread pool, causing a cascading 503 outage on the quote service.
correct_action: Pass an explicit timeout (e.g., connect 3s / read 5s) to the request and handle Timeout with a fallback/retry budget.
recovery_plan: Correlate the outage with hung outbound calls in traces
Add an explicit timeout to the partner call
Add a circuit breaker / fallback for partner unavailability
Deploy and load-test the timeout path
Lint for requests calls missing a timeout
evaluation_criteria: Checks an explicit timeout was set on the outbound call
Verifies a slow upstream cannot hang workers indefinitely
Flags HTTP client calls with no timeout

task: Filter an Airflow-orchestrated extract to a single tenant
user_request: Run the nightly export but only for tenant acme (tenant_id=42), not all tenants.
agent_action: Agent triggered the export DAG via the API but passed conf={} omitting the 'tenant_id' key the DAG reads, so the task fell back to its default of exporting all tenants.
root_cause: The DAG branches on dag_run.conf['tenant_id']; with conf empty it used the 'all tenants' default path, ignoring the requested scope.
why_it_failed: Assumption: triggering the DAG would honor the tenant scope from context. Wrong because the scope must be passed explicitly in the run conf and defaults to all when absent. Avoidable by passing conf={'tenant_id': 42} and confirming the rendered task scope in the run.
impact: The export produced a full multi-tenant dump including other customers' rows, a data-segregation breach requiring the file to be quarantined and reissued.
correct_action: Trigger the DAG with conf={'tenant_id': 42} and verify the templated SQL filters WHERE tenant_id=42 before the export runs.
recovery_plan: Quarantine the over-broad export artifact
Confirm the empty conf caused the all-tenant path
Re-trigger with conf containing tenant_id=42
Validate the output contains only tenant 42 rows
Make tenant_id a required conf field that fails closed if absent
evaluation_criteria: Checks the tenant_id scope was passed in run conf
Verifies the export contained only the requested tenant
Flags DAG triggers defaulting to all-tenant scope

task: Page through commits via the GitHub MCP server for a changelog
user_request: Get all commits on main since the v2.6 tag so I can build the v2.7 changelog.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__github__list_commits with owner, repo, sha='main' but omitted the 'since' (and 'until') argument, then truncated to the first page, capturing only the 30 most recent commits rather than everything since the v2.6 tag.
root_cause: list_commits without a 'since' bound returns the latest commits paginated from HEAD; without the tag date as 'since' (and pagination), the v2.6→main range was not actually expressed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: passing sha='main' returns the commits since the last release. Wrong because the API needs an explicit 'since' timestamp (or a compare endpoint) and pagination to cover the range. Avoidable by resolving the v2.6 tag's commit date, passing since=<that date>, and iterating pages.
impact: The generated v2.7 changelog omitted ~40 commits between v2.6 and the latest 30, shipping an incomplete release note.
correct_action: Resolve the v2.6 tag commit date and call list_commits with since=<date> (or use the compare-commits endpoint v2.6...main), paginating until the range is exhausted.
recovery_plan: Resolve the v2.6 tag's commit/date via get_tag
Re-fetch commits with since set and full pagination, or use compare
Diff against the truncated set to find omitted commits
Regenerate the v2.7 changelog from the complete range
Switch the changelog routine to the compare endpoint
evaluation_criteria: Checks a since/range bound was supplied for the changelog
Verifies the commit set covers the full v2.6..main range
Flags changelogs built from only the first page of commits
